transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-08-30
Start: 09:23 PDT
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Lena Park (Redwood AE), Markus Chen (Redwood SE), Priya Rao (Astra Ventures - Head of ML), Ethan Cole (Astra - SRE), Sofia Martinez (Astra - Data Scientist)

Summary:
Quick demo of Redwood's Eval & Quality Monitoring (Console + Optimize + API integration). Focus on prompt sets, regression alerts, and A/B comparison workflows. Discussed hosted vs dedicated for latency/cost tradeoffs and V P C deployment concerns. Agreed next steps: share pricing, security docs, run benchmark with sample prompt sets.

Topics:
- Prompt set management and sharing
- Regression detection and alerting thresholds
- A/B comparison and automatic rollbacks
- API instrumentation and SDK for evals
- Data residency / V P C private deployment concerns

Transcript body:
09:23 Lena: All right hey everyone thanks for making time, um we're gonna go through the evaluation and quality monitoring flow today, quick intro?
09:29 Priya: Hey thanks Lena, Priya here. we're really evaluating how to track prompt regressions across releases, and want something that ties to our alerts and S L A s.
09:34 Lena: Perfect, that's exactly what this demo's about. Markus will drive the Console and show how prompt sets and regressions work end-to-end.
09:39 Markus: Cool, i'll share my screen — i have the Redwood Console open, the Eval tab. Sorry if the transcriptions later calls it "Redwood Consolee" or something, notebook was noisy.
09:48 Ethan: Quick question before you share, we're particularly sensitive to token costs — we run a lot of batch jobs — curious how evals affect billing.
09:54 Markus: Yeah good call. you can run evals against cached responses or sampled production traffic to control cost; Optimize gives suggestions for batching and quantization profiles. For pilot we usually recommend sampling 1-5% of traffic for continuous monitoring, and full prompt-set runs as scheduled nightly.
10:06 Sofia: When you say prompt sets, can you show the format? we have multi-turn and structured outputs, sometimes JSON blobs in responses.
10:11 Markus: Absolutely — here's a sample prompt set in the UI. each row is: prompt id, description, reference / golden answer, metric(s) — e.g. exact-match, semantic-sim, hallucination-score. Also support for structured scoring where we can run JSON-schema validators to detect malformed outputs.
10:26 Priya: Are the metrics pluggable? we use custom F1 and a business score.
10:29 Markus: Yep, you can register custom metrics via the SDK or the API; we have a python client snippet — sorry the transcript might show wrong chars — but basically you push prompt sets and a scoring function.
10:38 Ethan: How are regression alerts surfaced? PagerDuty? Slack?
10:41 Markus: Integrations include Slack, PagerDuty, email, and webhooks. Alerts are rule-based, e.g. when avg semantic-sim drops below threshold for X prompts, or when A/B variant underperforms control by Y with statistical significance. You can tune sensitivity and noise floor — we also provide rolling baselines.
10:58 Priya: How do you handle A/B comparisons? our deployment flow has canaries and gradual rollouts — want automatic rollback if quality degrades.
11:03 Markus: The Console supports experiment definitions (A/B) tied to model versions or routing policies. You can define success metrics and set automatic actions: notify, pause rollout, or rollback. The auto-rollback uses permutation tests for significance; you can also require manual approval.
11:20 Sofia: Are we able to compare different quantized variants? e g the 8-bit vs 4-bit outputs for same model.
11:24 Markus: Yes — we treat model artifacts as variants; the eval platform can compare any two variants including different quantizations. Note: some low-precision variants may change hallucination patterns, so we recommend a prompt-specific QA threshold.
11:37 Priya: On compliance, we need audit logs and immutable records of eval runs for SOC2 reviews.
11:41 Lena: We provide run-level metadata, immutable logs, and exportable reports for audit. we also have RBAC and SSO (SAML) for who can trigger evals and modify thresholds.
11:53 Ethan: If we run in our V P C or on-premises, do the eval logs leave our network?
11:56 Lena: For Private deployments logs can stay inside your V P C; the control plane can be on Redwood or customer-managed depending on the contract. we'll share the architecture doc after the call — note we'll include K M S integration for keys.
12:08 Markus: Back to the demo — i'm going to run a quick prompt-set job. this one is a 120-prompt set, mixed bios and product descriptions, multi-turn. starting run now...
12:22 [transcription gap - audio glitch]
12:33 Markus: Ok looks like the batch run completed, here's the dashboard. you get per-prompt breakdown, time-to-first-token and median latency, token cost estimate, and a histogram of semantic-sim scores.
12:46 Priya: That cost estimate, is that from live token pricing or our negotiated rate?
12:49 Lena: In the Console it's based on list pricing; for Dedicated or committed pilots we'll apply your negotiated pricing, which we'll show in the invoice or pilot sheet.
12:56 Sofia: For the semantic sim we use embeddings — which embedding model do you use? we rely on high-quality embeddings for our scoring.
13:00 Markus: You can choose the embedding model in the eval job; we support Redwood-verified models and you can plug in your own. note embedding cost is separate and batched.
13:12 Priya: Do you support human-in-the-loop scoring so our labelers can override or flag cases?
13:16 Markus: Yes, there's an H I T L workflow: flag prompts, push to labeling queue, and incorporate human scores into thresholds. The system supports consensus and labeler weighting.
13:28 Ethan: Any examples of noisy transcripts? i mean in our logs we see ASR-derived prompts and want to avoid false alarms.
13:33 Markus: We surface confidence bands and allow ignoring low-confidence inputs; you can also segment by input channel.
13:40 Priya: About A/B stats — you mentioned permutation tests — is that robust to small sample sizes?
13:44 Markus: We fallback to bootstrap CIs when samples are small and add a minimum-sample gating rule. we show p-values but also effect sizes and credible intervals so you can make business decisions, not just p < 0.05.
13:56 Sofia: Will we be able to tag prompts with taxonomy? like "billing", "support", "onboarding" for aggregated views?
14:00 Markus: Yes taggable prompt-sets and nested folders in the Console. you can build dashboards scoped to tag(s).
14:10 Priya: Ok practical question — we have a nightly model release cadence. we'd like nightly eval runs plus continuous monitors; what's the recommended config for a team our size (we're ~40 ML engineers, medium traffic)?
14:18 Lena: For that size we recommend daily full prompt-set runs for critical flows, plus continuous sampling on production at 2% for regression detection. consider Dedicated capacity if median latency under 120ms is a hard requirement, otherwise Hosted with pinned variants + autoscale is often fine.
14:30 Ethan: For Dedicated do we get guaranteed GPU types? we use A100s on-prem and want parity.
14:34 Lena: Dedicated contracts let you specify GPU class and throughput targets; we can match A100-equivalent profiles depending on region and availability.
14:44 Priya: The last bit — integrations: can we push alerts to our existing internal dashboard (custom endpoint)?
14:47 Markus: Webhook integration supports a JSON payload with run summary; you can ingest that into your dashboard. for high-throughput alerts we recommend batching notifications.
14:54 [brief cross talk]
15:02 Lena: Cool — time to recap next steps. we'll send pilot pricing and the security pack, Markus will prepare the benchmarking plan and run checklist, and Priya will share prompt sets.
15:12 Priya: sounds good, i'll try to send the prompt sets by Tuesday.
15:16 Ethan: i'll coordinate SRE requirements and share the network runbook for V P C by end of week.
15:21 Lena: thanks everyone, i'll put calendar invites for the benchmarking slot once Markus and Priya agree on times.
15:26 Markus: One last note — we can seed the pilot with a lightweight A/B comparing your current hosted model vs a quantized variant and generate regression alerts during the pilot, want us to include that?
15:34 Priya: Yes please include that in the benchmark plan.
15:37 Lena: Great, thanks all. we'll follow up with docs and a proposal. bye.
15:40 [call ended]

Post-call notes:
- Transcript contains occasional auto-caption errors (e g "Consolee", "K V cache", "V P C") typical of call transcription.
- Agreed pilot scope: 2-week trial including daily full prompt-set runs and continuous sampling, A/B comparison across quantization variants, and SOC2 audit artifacts for eval runs.
- Items to attach: architecture doc (private deployment), SOC2 pack, pilot pricing sheet, prompt-set template, benchmarking checklist.
